disease_label_per_paper: Normal lipase serum level in acute pancreatitis with CT-confirmed pancreatitis and gallstones
presentation_summary: 84-year-old man presented with 24 hours of recurrent diffuse abdominal pain and vomiting.
History included type 1 diabetes mellitus, dysarthria and left hemiplegia after ischemic stroke, prior operation for suspected bowel sepsis, bladder polyps, and left nephrectomy.
He was afebrile at 36.9 C with blood pressure 152/90 mmHg, heart rate 116/min, moderate tachypnea, jaundice, abdominal distension, and diffuse abdominal pain.

Labs included WBC 11.9 x 10^9/L, CRP 169 mg/L, creatinine 261 umol/L, glucose 31.7 mmol/L, pH 7.39, CO2/bicarbonate 19 mmol/L, bilirubin 88 umol/L, GGT 1040 U/L, ALP 156 U/L, AST 38 U/L, ALT 128 U/L, LDH 1014 U/L, and normal lipase 44 U/L.
CT revealed acute inflammation of the pancreas and peripancreatic fat with fluid collection and gallstones; subsequent lipase readings remained normal until after ERCP.
